# 1 Kings Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Now when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD, she came to test him with hard questions.
**2** She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels bearing spices and very much gold and precious stones. And when she came to Solomon, she told him all that was on her mind.
**3** And Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from the king that he could not explain to her.
**4** And when the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,
**5** the food of his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he offered at the house of the LORD, there was no more breath in her.
**6** And she said to the king, "The report was true that I heard in my own land of your words and of your wisdom.
**7** I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes had seen it. And behold, the half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity surpass the report that I heard.
**8** Happy are your men! Happy are your servants, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!
**9** Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! Because the LORD loved Israel forever, he has made you king, that you may execute justice and righteousness."
**10** Then she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as these that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
**11** Moreover, the fleet of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a very great amount of almug wood and precious stones.
**12** And the king made of the almug wood supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, also lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day.
**13** And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides what was given her by the bounty of King Solomon. So she turned and went back to her own land with her servants.
**14** Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
**15** besides that which came from the traders and from the business of the merchants, and from all the kings of Arabia and from the governors of the land.
**16** King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield.
**17** And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
**18** The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with the finest gold.
**19** The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round at the back, and on each side of the seat were armrests, and two lions stood beside the armrests,
**20** while twelve lions stood there, one on each end of a step on the six steps. The like of it was never made in any kingdom.
**21** All King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None were of silver; silver was not considered as anything in the days of Solomon.
**22** For the king had a fleet of ships of Tarshish at sea with the fleet of Hiram. Once every three years the fleet of ships of Tarshish used to come bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
**23** Thus King Solomon excelled all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
**24** And the whole earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put into his mind.
**25** Every one of them brought his present: articles of silver and gold, garments, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules, so much year by year.
**26** And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
**27** And the king made silver as common as stone in Jerusalem, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore of the Shephelah.
**28** And Solomon's import of horses was from Egypt and Kue, and the king's traders received them from Kue at a price.
**29** A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred and fifty, and so through the king's traders they were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

**Key Observations**:
- EMET preserves Hebrew word order and particles (ʾet, vav-consecutive) that reveal syntactic emphasis
- LOGOS provides the most balanced English rendering suitable for study
- PNEUMA's dynamic approach often captures emotional register and narrative pacing most effectively

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Chapter 10**: 23 verse(s) with significant divergence

### Verse 2
- **EMET**: And-she-came to-Jerusalem with-a-very great retinue — camels carrying spices and-gold in-great-abundance and-precious stones. And-she-came to Solomon and-spoke to-him ʾet-all that was on her-heart.
- **LOGOS**: She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels bearing spices and very much gold and precious stones. And when she came to Solomon, she told him all that was on her mind.
- **PNEUMA**: She arrived in Jerusalem with a massive entourage: camels loaded with spices, enormous quantities of gold, and precious stones. When she met Solomon, she posed every question she had prepared.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 3
- **EMET**: And-Solomon told-her ʾet-all her-words; there-was-not a-thing hidden from the-king that he-did-not tell-her.
- **LOGOS**: And Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from the king that he could not explain to her.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon answered every one. Nothing was too complex for the king to explain.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 4
- **EMET**: And-the-queen-of Sheba saw ʾet-all the-wisdom-of Solomon and-the-house that he-built,
- **LOGOS**: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,
- **PNEUMA**: When the queen of Sheba saw the full extent of Solomon's wisdom, the palace he had built,
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 5
- **EMET**: and-the-food-of his-table and-the-seating-of his-servants and-the-standing-of his-attendants and-their-clothing and-his-cupbearers, and-his-burnt-offering that he-offered at-the-house-of YHWH — and-th...
- **LOGOS**: the food of his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and his burnt offerings that he offered at the house of the LORD, there was no more...
- **PNEUMA**: the food on his table, how his officials were seated, how his servants stood at attention in their uniforms, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the LORD's temple — it took her bre...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 7
- **EMET**: And-I-did-not believe the-words until I-came and-my-eyes saw — and-behold, the-half was-not told to-me. You-have-added wisdom and-good beyond the-report that I-heard.
- **LOGOS**: I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes had seen it. And behold, the half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity surpass the report that I heard.
- **PNEUMA**: I didn't believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. In fact, I wasn't told even half of it. Your wisdom and wealth far exceed the reports I heard.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 8
- **EMET**: Happy are your-men; happy are these your-servants who-stand before-you continually, who-hear ʾet-your-wisdom.
- **LOGOS**: Happy are your men! Happy are your servants, who continually stand before you and hear your wisdom!
- **PNEUMA**: How fortunate your people are! How fortunate these servants of yours, who stand in your presence every day and hear your wisdom!
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 9
- **EMET**: Blessed is YHWH your-God, who delighted in-you, to-set-you on the-throne-of Israel. Because-of-the-love-of YHWH for-Israel forever, he-made-you king, to-do justice and-righteousness."
- **LOGOS**: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel! Because the LORD loved Israel forever, he has made you king, that you may execute justice and righteousness....
- **PNEUMA**: Praise be to the LORD your God, who has taken such delight in you that he placed you on the throne of Israel. Because the LORD's love for Israel is eternal, he has made you king to uphold justice and ...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 10
- **EMET**: And-she-gave to-the-king a-hundred and-twenty talents-of gold and-spices in-very-great abundance, and-precious stones. There-never came again such abundance-of spices as-that which the-queen-of Sheba ...
- **LOGOS**: Then she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again came such an abundance of spices as these that the queen of Sheba ga...
- **PNEUMA**: She gave the king 120 talents of gold, a huge quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again did such a quantity of spices arrive as what the queen of Sheba gave Solomon.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 11
- **EMET**: And-also the-fleet-of Hiram that carried gold from-Ophir brought from-Ophir almug wood in-great-abundance and-precious stones.
- **LOGOS**: Moreover, the fleet of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a very great amount of almug wood and precious stones.
- **PNEUMA**: Hiram's fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought large shipments of almug wood and precious stones.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 12
- **EMET**: And-the-king made from-the-almug wood supports for-the-house-of YHWH and-for-the-house-of the-king, and-lyres and-harps for-the-singers. Such almug wood has-not come nor-been-seen to this day.
- **LOGOS**: And the king made of the almug wood supports for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, also lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug wood has come or been seen to this day.
- **PNEUMA**: The king used the almug wood to make railings for the LORD's temple and the royal palace, and lyres and harps for the musicians. No such shipment of almug wood has ever arrived since.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 13
- **EMET**: And-the-king Solomon gave to-the-queen-of Sheba ʾet-all her-desire, that she-asked, besides what he-gave-her according-to-the-hand-of the-king Solomon. And-she-turned and-went to-her-land — she and-he...
- **LOGOS**: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides what was given her by the bounty of King Solomon. So she turned and went back to her own land with her ser...
- **PNEUMA**: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted — whatever she asked for — in addition to the royal gifts he gave her from his own generosity. Then she returned home with her attendants.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 14
- **EMET**: And-the-weight-of the-gold that came to-Solomon in-one year was six-hundred and-sixty-six talents-of gold,
- **LOGOS**: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
- **PNEUMA**: The weight of gold Solomon received in a single year was 666 talents,
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 15
- **EMET**: besides that from the-men-of the-traders and-the-profit-of the-merchants and-all the-kings-of the-mixed-peoples and-the-governors-of the-land.
- **LOGOS**: besides that which came from the traders and from the business of the merchants, and from all the kings of Arabia and from the governors of the land.
- **PNEUMA**: not counting revenue from merchants, traders, all the Arabian kings, and the regional governors.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 17
- **EMET**: And-three-hundred shields-of beaten gold — three minas-of gold went on each shield. And-the-king put-them in-the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon.
- **LOGOS**: And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
- **PNEUMA**: He also made three hundred smaller shields of hammered gold, using three minas of gold for each. He placed them in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 19
- **EMET**: Six steps had-the-throne, and-a-round-top to-the-throne from-behind-it, and-armrests on-each-side by-the-place-of sitting, and-two lions standing beside the-armrests.
- **LOGOS**: The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round at the back, and on each side of the seat were armrests, and two lions stood beside the armrests,
- **PNEUMA**: The throne had six steps, with a rounded back. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing on each side.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 20
- **EMET**: And-twelve lions standing there on the-six steps, on-each-side. Nothing like-it was-made for-any kingdom.
- **LOGOS**: while twelve lions stood there, one on each end of a step on the six steps. The like of it was never made in any kingdom.
- **PNEUMA**: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each end. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 21
- **EMET**: And-all the-drinking-vessels-of the-king Solomon were-of gold, and-all the-vessels-of the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon were-of refined gold. None were-of silver — it-was-not reckoned as-anything in-...
- **LOGOS**: All King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. None were of silver; silver was not considered as anything in the days of...
- **PNEUMA**: All of Solomon's drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Nothing was made of silver — silver was considered worthless in Solomon's day.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 23
- **EMET**: And-the-king Solomon was-greater than-all the-kings-of the-earth in-riches and-in-wisdom.
- **LOGOS**: Thus King Solomon excelled all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
- **PNEUMA**: King Solomon surpassed every king on earth in wealth and wisdom.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 24
- **EMET**: And-all the-earth was-seeking ʾet-the-face-of Solomon, to-hear ʾet-his-wisdom that God had-put in-his-heart.
- **LOGOS**: And the whole earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put into his mind.
- **PNEUMA**: The whole world wanted an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had given him.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 25
- **EMET**: And-they — each-one bringing his-gift: vessels-of silver and-vessels-of gold, and-garments, and-armor, and-spices, horses and-mules — the-matter-of each-year in-its-year.
- **LOGOS**: Every one of them brought his present: articles of silver and gold, garments, myrrh, spices, horses, and mules, so much year by year.
- **PNEUMA**: Year after year, each visitor brought gifts — silver and gold articles, robes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 26
- **EMET**: And-Solomon gathered chariots and-horsemen. And-he-had a-thousand and-four-hundred chariots and-twelve-thousand horsemen. And-he-placed-them in-the-chariot-cities and-with the-king in-Jerusalem.
- **LOGOS**: And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon amassed fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he stationed in chariot cities and with him in Jerusalem.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 28
- **EMET**: And-the-export-of horses that Solomon had was from-Egypt and-from-Kue — the-traders-of the-king would-take-them from-Kue at-a-price.
- **LOGOS**: And Solomon's import of horses was from Egypt and Kue, and the king's traders received them from Kue at a price.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and Kue. The royal traders purchased them from Kue at the going rate.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 29
- **EMET**: And-a-chariot came-up and-went-out from-Egypt for-six-hundred shekels-of silver, and-a-horse for-a-hundred and-fifty. And-so for-all the-kings-of the-Hittites and-the-kings-of Aram — by-their-hand the...
- **LOGOS**: A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred and fifty, and so through the king's traders they were exported to all the kings of the Hittites an...
- **PNEUMA**: A chariot from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse one hundred and fifty. They were also exported through Solomon's agents to the Hittite and Aramean kings.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

— SOPHIA
